thread:
incident-bot: [P1] TLS handshake failure surge for prod-api (us-east-2). 5xx TLS errors = 12.1% over 5m. Auto-paging oncall.

Harper (oncall): I'm on the page. Paging Ethan and Diego. Zoe, any customer-visible errors?

Zoe (Support): yes, several APAC and EU customers reporting 502/503s. Ticket #8124 includes edge log lines: 'ssl_handshake: alert handshake failure' and a customer's curl -v showing 'certificate verify failed'.

Ethan (SRE): frontend alert stream shows many TLS handshake failures starting ~10m ago. Two infra changes within the hour: an automated cert rotation finished ~40m ago and an infra change to the transit gateway (VXLAN encapsulation update) ~25m ago that adjusted encapsulation overhead. Could be correlated.

Diego (NetEng): during TGW maintenance we changed VXLAN encapsulation settings which increased overhead; one intermediate router is now advertising pmtu 1476 (was 1500). That can cause large ClientHello packets to be fragmented or dropped depending on DF/ICMP path behavior.

Harper (oncall): timeline so far:
- 04:05 UTC: cert rotation job ran
- 04:28 UTC: TGW VXLAN encapsulation update completed (new overhead applied)
- 04:40 UTC: handshake errors begin climbing
- 04:45 UTC: incident-bot paged oncall

Ethan (SRE): sample nginx errors from frontend pool alpha:
```
2026-03-22T04:45:18Z error nginx[frontend-alpha]: *78 ssl_handshake: TLSv1.2 alert handshake failure while SSL handshaking, client: 10.55.11.72, server: 10.2.14.9
2026-03-22T04:45:18Z warn nginx[frontend-alpha]: *78 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while connecting to upstream, client: 10.55.11.72, server: 10.2.14.9
```

Zoe (Support): attached user's curl trace (EU):
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/healthz
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (18.212.33.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
```

Diego (NetEng): tcpdump snippet from edge ENI shows ICMP frag-needed with mtu=1476. excerpt:
```
04:39:58.123000 IP 10.55.11.72 > 18.212.33.5: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0], length 0
04:39:58.123050 IP 172.40.7.1 > 10.55.11.72: ICMP frag-needed and DF set, mtu 1476
```
Also seeing some asymmetric ICMP behavior on a subset of paths where frag-needed gets dropped.

Ethan (SRE): another data point: openssl check against a rotated host 10.2.14.9:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.2.14.9:443 -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000005)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood.example.com
   i:/CN=Intermediate-CA
```
This host's keystore appears to be missing the intermediate certificate in the PKCS12 bundle (rotation job packaged cert-only). I can reproduce on 10.2.14.9 and 10.2.14.10; 10.2.14.11 shows full chain.

Zoe (Support): so two simultaneous issues: a network MTU/fragmentation problem causing some clients to fail mid-handshake plus a subset of hosts lacking the intermediate cert which causes verify failures for clients that don't have the chain cached. Compound effect matches the sudden spike.

Diego (NetEng): tracepath to 18.212.33.5 shows pmtu 1476 at hop 2:
```
$ tracepath -n 18.212.33.5
 1: 10.55.11.1       0.412ms pmtu 1500
 2: 172.40.7.1       1.024ms pmtu 1476
 3: 18.212.33.5      7.856ms pmtu 1476
```
If client TLS ClientHello > 1476, it will be fragmented or trigger ICMP frag-needed. Some networks strip those ICMPs leading to PMTU blackholes and dropped fragments. That would break TLS handshakes unpredictably.

Ethan (SRE): hypotheses (in-thread):
- H1 (confirmed): PMTU mismatch introduced by VXLAN overhead change on TGW causing fragment drops on some paths -> evidence: icmp frag-needed in tcpdump, tracepath pmtu 1476, asymmetry on some paths. Mitigation: temporary MSS clamp on TGW route table and alternative route via older encapsulation.
- H2 (confirmed): rotation job failed to include intermediate cert in PKCS12 on a subset of frontends -> evidence: openssl verify error on some hosts; rollback to keystore backup restores chain. Mitigation: rollback affected keystores and patch rotation pipeline to validate chain.
- H3 (investigating): clients with large SNI or early TLS extensions produce oversized ClientHello that are more susceptible. We'll try to reproduce with large SNI and session ticket sizes in lab.

Harper (oncall): immediate actions: Ethan roll back keystore for 10.2.14.9/10 and reload nginx gracefully. Diego apply MSS clamp at TGW to MSS=1440 (safe below 1476 minus typical overhead) and add an alternative route avoiding VXLAN for critical egress. Zoe craft customer message: mitigation in progress.

runbook-bot: restore-keystore initiated for 10.2.14.9 (backup: keystore-backups/2026-03-22-03:50)

Ethan (SRE): keystore restore complete on 10.2.14.9; reloaded nginx with 'systemctl reload nginx'. early logs show certificate chain validated: 
```
2026-03-22T04:48:02Z info nginx[frontend-alpha]: SSL: certificate chain validated for CN=api.redwood.example.com
```
Rolling restore to 10.2.14.10 now.

Diego (NetEng): applied MSS clamp to TGW route table rtb-0xabc123 (MSS=1440). Also injected a temporary BGP policy to prefer non-VXLAN path for client-facing egress subnets. Monitoring ICMP counters; seeing frag-needed messages drop and successful retransmits increase.

Harper (oncall): monitoring metrics: TLS handshake errors down 12.1% -> 2.4% within 6 minutes. Customer tickets decreasing. Good progress.

Zoe (Support): outbound message to affected customers: "We've applied mitigations: restored missing certificate chain on affected frontends and a temporary network workaround to avoid packet fragmentation. Engineers are collecting artifacts for a full RCA and will follow up shortly." :thumbsup:

Ethan (SRE): in-thread artifact tracker and next steps:
- Artifacts collected: nginx error logs (frontend-alpha), tcpdump captures (edge ENI 04:39:58), tracepath outputs, openssl outputs, runbook logs. Attached logs will be archived to incident-1780000000.
- Follow-ups: patch cert rotation pipeline to perform automated openssl s_client chain validation across a canary set before wide rollout; ensure PKCS12 export includes full chain. Add automated keystore rollback on chain-mismatch detection.

Diego (NetEng): network follow-ups: revert VXLAN overhead change or adjust encapsulation MTU advertise to match internal expectations; update TGW config to advertise correct PMTU; add alerting for ICMP frag-needed spikes; add automated MSS-clamp playbook to the runbook. Ticket TGW-256 opened.

Ethan (SRE): hypothesis status updated:
- H1 (confirmed): PMTU mismatch / VXLAN overhead change caused mid-handshake fragmentation -> evidence attached (tcpdump, tracepath).
- H2 (confirmed): cert chain omission from rotation created verify failures on subset -> evidence attached (openssl outputs), fixed by keystore restore.
- H3 (open): large ClientHello edge cases may exacerbate problem. Will attempt lab reproduction using varied SNI and ticket sizes.

Harper (oncall): handing incident to Ethan for RCA writeup and action tracking. I'll remain reachable for escalations until RCA published.

Zoe (Support): I'll notify affected customers with RCA ETA and provide rollback confirmation.

incident-bot: severity downgraded to P2 based on reduced user impact and mitigation progress.

Ethan (SRE): final note in-thread: please upload any extra pcap files (interface + timestamp), full PKCS12 exports, and any client traces here; I'll bundle into the RCA and schedule a 30m postmortem to review action owners and timelines.
